Here's a well-structured systemd service unit file along with the companion check script:

---

### `/etc/systemd/system/config-check.service`

```ini
[Unit]
Description=System Configuration Check
Documentation=man:systemd.service(5)
After=network.target
Wants=network.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/config-check.sh
User=root
Group=root

# Safety hardening
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=read-only
PrivateTmp=true
ReadWritePaths=/var/log/config-check

# Output capture
StandardOutput=journal
StandardError=journal
SyslogIdentifier=config-check

# On failure, don't restart — alert instead
Restart=no
RemainAfterExit=yes

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

---

### `/usr/local/bin/config-check.sh`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# config-check.sh — System configuration validation script
set -euo pipefail

LOG_DIR="/var/log/config-check"
LOG_FILE="${LOG_DIR}/config-check.log"
TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
FAIL=0

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"

log() {
  local level="$1"; shift
  echo "[$TIMESTAMP] [$level] $*" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
}

check() {
  local label="$1"
  local result="$2"  # "ok" or "fail"
  local detail="$3"
  if [[ "$result" == "ok" ]]; then
    log INFO  "✔ $label — $detail"
  else
    log ERROR "✘ $label — $detail"
    FAIL=1
  fi
}

log INFO "=== Config check started ==="

# 1. SSH root login disabled
ssh_root=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null | grep -i "^permitrootlogin" | awk '{print $2}' || echo "unknown")
[[ "$ssh_root" == "no" ]] \
  && check "SSH root login" ok "PermitRootLogin=no" \
  || check "SSH root login" fail "PermitRootLogin=$ssh_root (expected: no)"

# 2. Firewall active (ufw or firewalld)
if command -v ufw &>/dev/null; then
  ufw_status=$(ufw status | head -1 | awk '{print $2}')
  [[ "$ufw_status" == "active" ]] \
    && check "UFW firewall" ok "active" \
    || check "UFW firewall" fail "status=$ufw_status"
elif command -v firewall-cmd &>/dev/null; then
  fw_state=$(firewall-cmd --state 2>/dev/null || echo "not running")
  [[ "$fw_state" == "running" ]] \
    && check "firewalld" ok "running" \
    || check "firewalld" fail "state=$fw_state"
else
  check "Firewall" fail "neither ufw nor firewalld found"
fi

# 3. Unattended upgrades / automatic updates enabled
if dpkg -l unattended-upgrades &>/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ua_conf="/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades"
  if grep -q "Unattended-Upgrade \"1\"" "$ua_conf" 2>/dev/null; then
    check "Unattended upgrades" ok "enabled"
  else
    check "Unattended upgrades" fail "not enabled in $ua_conf"
  fi
else
  check "Unattended upgrades" fail "package not installed"
fi

# 4. Password aging configured
max_days=$(grep "^PASS_MAX_DAYS" /etc/login.defs | awk '{print $2}')
[[ "${max_days:-0}" -le 90 && "${max_days:-0}" -gt 0 ]] \
  && check "Password max age" ok "${max_days} days" \
  || check "Password max age" fail "PASS_MAX_DAYS=${max_days:-unset} (should be ≤90)"

# 5. Core dumps disabled
core_limit=$(ulimit -c 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
[[ "$core_limit" == "0" ]] \
  && check "Core dumps" ok "disabled" \
  || check "Core dumps" fail "limit=$core_limit (expected: 0)"

log INFO "=== Config check complete ==="

if [[ "$FAIL" -ne 0 ]]; then
  log ERROR "One or more checks FAILED. Review $LOG_FILE"
  exit 1
fi

log INFO "All checks passed."
exit 0
```

---

### Setup commands

```bash
# Install the script
sudo cp config-check.sh /usr/local/bin/config-check.sh
sudo chmod 700 /usr/local/bin/config-check.sh

# Install the unit file
sudo cp config-check.service /etc/systemd/system/config-check.service

# Reload systemd and enable/run
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable config-check.service   # run at boot
sudo systemctl start config-check.service    # run now

# Check results
sudo systemctl status config-check.service
sudo journalctl -u config-check.service
sudo cat /var/log/config-check/config-check.log
```

---

### Key design decisions

| Choice | Reason |
|---|---|
| `Type=oneshot` | Runs once and exits — appropriate for a check/audit script |
| `RemainAfterExit=yes` | Keeps the unit in "active" state so `systemctl status` shows pass/fail |
| `ProtectSystem=strict` + `PrivateTmp` | Sandboxes the service; `ReadWritePaths` carves out just the log dir |
| `Restart=no` | A failed check shouldn't loop — you want to fix the config, not retry endlessly |
| `SyslogIdentifier` | Makes `journalctl -u config-check` output clean and filterable |

Add a timer unit (`config-check.timer`) if you want this to run on a schedule rather than just at boot.

Here's a precise breakdown of how each requirement is satisfied:

---

### ✅ Root privileges — `[Service]` section

```ini
User=root
Group=root
```

This explicitly runs the service process as `root:root`. No ambiguity — systemd will not drop privileges before exec'ing the script.

> **Note on `NoNewPrivileges=true`:** This is kept intentionally. It doesn't *remove* root access — it just prevents the script from spawning child processes that escalate *beyond* root (e.g. via setuid binaries). It's a safety rail, not a restriction on root itself.

---

### ✅ Auto-start at boot — `[Install]` section

```ini
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

This is the key piece. When you run:

```bash
sudo systemctl enable config-check.service
```

systemd creates a symlink in `/etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/`, which causes the service to be pulled in automatically every time the system reaches **multi-user mode** (the standard fully-booted, non-graphical target — equivalent to runlevel 3).

---

### Boot order guarantee — `[Unit]` section

```ini
After=network.target
Wants=network.target
```

This ensures the service starts *after* the network is up, so any config checks involving network services (SSH, firewall, etc.) have a stable environment to inspect.

---

### Full enable + verify sequence

```bash
# Deploy
sudo cp config-check.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload

# Enable auto-start at boot
sudo systemctl enable config-check.service
# → Creates: /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/config-check.service

# Confirm it's enabled
sudo systemctl is-enabled config-check.service
# → enabled

# Confirm it will run as root
sudo systemctl show config-check.service | grep -E "^User=|^Group="
# → User=root
# → Group=root

# Trigger a manual run to verify before next reboot
sudo systemctl start config-check.service
sudo systemctl status config-check.service
```

Everything is in place — root execution and boot-time auto-start are both fully configured.
